_what: The Live Room: a recording studio on the street, seen from the control room, over the desk, through the glass. Sessions played in a studio -- a television studio, a radio station's live room -- rather than at a gig. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-25: a room for Live In Studio sets, starting with the Austin City Limits tapings that could not go on Looming Rocks, then KEXP and KCRW, the same afternoon, with other studios to follow. Nothing is hosted here and nothing is fetched until somebody presses something.
_where_from: THE FIRST STUDIO ARRIVED BY WAY OF ANOTHER ROOM. Ryan sent ten Austin City Limits videos for Looming Rocks on 2026-09-25, in the same message that made Looming Rocks the room for outdoor music. One was a festival set in Zilker Park and went there. The other nine are the television series, taped indoors, and Looming Rocks refuses an act that was not played outdoors -- so they were held, and the same afternoon Ryan asked for this room to hold them. make-live-room.py refuses a session that was NOT played indoors, which is make-looming.py's rule upside down: the two rooms keep the same promise about where a thing was played, and must not be made to agree.
_ids: EVERY ID WAS CHECKED ON ITS OWN WATCH PAGE, NOT REMEMBERED. All nine were opened on 2026-09-25 and read for playabilityStatus, playableInEmbed and lengthSeconds, and all nine answer OK and true; none is age-gated. The runtimes below are the measured lengthSeconds, and the titles, channels and dates are read off each video's own title and description. Where a date or a venue is not in the description it is not on the page. The thirteen KEXP sessions were checked the same way on 2026-09-25: every one OK, embeddable, on KEXP's own channel, and every description says it was performed in the KEXP studio and gives the date it was recorded. The seven KCRW sessions were checked the same way on 2026-09-25: every one OK, embeddable and on KCRW's own channel, and every description names the studio it was played in -- KCRW's own performance studio, Apogee Studio, or The Village Studios -- all indoors. Only two give a year, and only those two strips carry one.
_acl: AUSTIN CITY LIMITS IS CREDITED AS SOMEBODY ELSE'S. The longest-running music series in American television, made by KLRU-TV in Austin and broadcast on PBS; its pilot was shot on 17 October 1974 with Willie Nelson. It was taped at KLRU's Studio 6A on the University of Texas campus for its first thirty-six seasons, and has been taped at ACL Live at The Moody Theater in downtown Austin since its first taping there on 26 February 2011. Read off en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_City_Limits on 2026-09-25, and the 1974 start is also in the show's own descriptions. THE LIVE ROOM IS NOT EITHER OF THOSE ROOMS, and Stimpunks has no connection to the show, KLRU or PBS.
_uploads: FOUR OF THE NINE ARE ON AUSTIN CITY LIMITS' OWN CHANNEL, which is the most durable shape of upload this room carries. The other five are on channels that collect recordings; two of them say in their own descriptions that the recording is not theirs. They are named on every strip rather than tidied away, because none of this music is ours and the channel is the most useful thing to know when one of them stops playing. THE STEVIE RAY VAUGHAN UPLOAD IS TITLED A FULL CONCERT AND IS NOT ONE: its own description lists six songs cut from it, and its strip says so before the press, beside the runtime, because the runtime is only honest if the reader knows what it is the runtime of.

studios.name: Austin City Limits
studios.about: A television studio with a crowd in it: the longest-running music series in American television, made by KLRU in Austin for PBS since 1974. Its first thirty-six seasons were taped in Studio 6A on the University of Texas campus, in front of a painted skyline of the city; since 2011 it has been taped at ACL Live at The Moody Theater, downtown. Every strip says which of the two it was.

sessions.title: Billy Strings on Austin City Limits
sessions.note: Bluegrass on fiddle, banjo, mandolin, bass and guitar: songs off Highway Prayers beside older tunes, with two long runs where one goes straight into the next without stopping. An interview after the last song, before the credits.

sessions.title: Cassandra Wilson on Austin City Limits
sessions.note: A set of songs Billie Holiday sang, made for her hundredth birthday and put out again by the show in 2026. It ends on an encore, and there is an interview after it.

sessions.title: Brandi Carlile: the Hall of Fame episode
sessions.note: The hour the show gave her when she went into its Hall of Fame. The first fourteen minutes are a tribute film, Bonnie Raitt inducting her and her own speech; the set starts after that, centred on Returning to Myself, and Raitt comes back out for one song near the end.

sessions.title: Tedeschi Trucks Band on Austin City Limits, 2016
sessions.note: A big band on one stage: two drummers, horns, backing singers, and two guitarists who are married to each other.

sessions.title: Stevie Ray Vaughan & Double Trouble on Austin City Limits, 1989
sessions.note: Titled a full concert and not one: the uploader's own description lists six songs cut from it, so the runtime on this strip is the runtime of what is left. What is left is the band in the old studio, in front of the painted skyline, the year before Vaughan died.

sessions.title: John Prine on Austin City Limits, 2005
sessions.note: Prine with three other players, and a set that reaches from his first record to the one he was touring then. It runs well past the broadcast hour.

sessions.title: Merle Haggard on Austin City Limits, 1978
sessions.note: Four years into the show, and taped before the painted skyline went up behind the stage in 1982: the studio as it was at the start.

sessions.title: Leonard Cohen on Austin City Limits, 1988
sessions.note: His first time on the show, taped on Halloween night 1988 on the I'm Your Man tour and first broadcast the next year.

sessions.title: Steve Miller Band on Austin City Limits, 2011
sessions.note: From the first year in the new theater, and well past the broadcast hour: the uploader's setlist runs through the band's hits with a stretch of blues in the middle.

studios.name: KEXP
studios.about: A listener-supported radio station in Seattle, with its studios at the Seattle Center and a live room that bands come through to play a short set on air. Every session on its channel says who played what, who hosted, and who engineered, mixed and filmed it; the strips here carry the date it was recorded and who hosted.

sessions.title: Screaming Females on KEXP
sessions.note: A trio: Marissa Paternoster on guitar and vocals, Michael Abbate on bass, Jarrett Dougherty on drums. Four songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters.

sessions.title: The Bobby Lees on KEXP
sessions.note: A four-piece fronted by Sam Quartin, hosted by Brian Foss. The last of the five runs one song straight into another.

sessions.title: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard on KEXP, 2022
sessions.note: Six of them, and three songs long enough to fill three quarters of an hour. Mixed by the band's own Stu Mackenzie, as their other visits beside it were.

sessions.title: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard on KEXP, 2019
sessions.note: Five songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters and mixed by Stu Mackenzie. The same band in the same room three years before the strip beside it, and two years after the one on the other side.

sessions.title: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard on KEXP, 2017
sessions.note: Four songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters and mixed by Stu Mackenzie: the same band in the same room five years before the first of these three strips.

sessions.title: Die Spitz on KEXP
sessions.note: A four-piece in which two of the players swap between guitar and drums. Four songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters.

sessions.title: Panic Shack on KEXP
sessions.note: Five of them, three on guitars and bass singing along behind Sarah Harvey. Five songs, hosted by Brian Foss.

sessions.title: Faetooth on KEXP
sessions.note: A trio, two of them singing, and four songs that take their time. Hosted by Tanner Ellison.

sessions.title: Built To Spill on KEXP
sessions.note: Doug Martsch with Teresa Esguerra on drums and Melanie Radford on bass. Four songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters.

sessions.title: AURORA on KEXP
sessions.note: Aurora Aksnes with a band of four, three of them singing behind her, and her own engineers alongside the station's. Four songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters.

sessions.title: Thievery Corporation on KEXP
sessions.note: Five songs, hosted by Darek Mazzone, in the autumn of 2016.

sessions.title: Waxahatchee on KEXP
sessions.note: Katie Crutchfield with a band of five, pedal steel, dobro and banjo among them, and one cover in the four songs. Hosted by Cheryl Waters.

sessions.title: Prewn on KEXP
sessions.note: A five-piece with a cello in it, fronted by Izzy Hagerup. Five songs, hosted by Cheryl Waters.

studios.name: KCRW
studios.about: A non-profit public radio station in Santa Monica. Some of its sessions are played in the performance studio at its own headquarters and some in other studios, and every strip says which; the descriptions on its channel credit the players and the whole crew by name.

sessions.title: Wet Leg, Live From KCRW HQ
sessions.note: A five-piece from the Isle of Wight, every one of them singing, fronted by Rhian Teasdale. Five songs.

sessions.title: Alabama Shakes on KCRW, 2015
sessions.note: Brittany Howard and the band, nine songs, played for KCRW to mark the release of Sound & Color.

sessions.title: Courtney Barnett, Live on KCRW
sessions.note: Songs off Creature of Habit, with Stella Mozgawa on drums and Zach Dawes on bass. She has played that studio before, by KCRW's own account.

sessions.title: Tears for Fears, Live from The Village Studios
sessions.note: Songs off The Tipping Point beside older ones, in a recording studio rather than the station's own.

sessions.title: Silvana Estrada, Live From KCRW HQ
sessions.note: Songs off Vendrán Suaves Lluvias, sung in Spanish, with Estrada on the four-string Venezuelan cuatro and strings, piano and woodwinds around her.

sessions.title: Kokoroko, Live From KCRW HQ
sessions.note: Seven of them, led by Sheila Maurice-Grey on trumpet and Onome Edgeworth on percussion, playing four songs off Tuff Times Never Last. Hosted by Novena Carmel.

sessions.title: Norah Jones on KCRW, 2016
sessions.note: Eight songs, several of them off Day Breaks.
